title: NATO-IP4 Relations Remain Stronger Than the Last Two Summits Suggest
author: Mirna Galic
text:
The chiefs of defense of the United States, Australia, Japan, New Zealand, and South Korea attend a session on “Partners in the Indo-Pacific” at the 194th NATO Military Committee in Chiefs of Defense session in Brussels, Belgium, Jan. 22, 2026.
Credit: NATO
A notable feature of the July 2026 NATO Summit in Ankara was the absence, for the second year in a row, of the four leaders of NATO’s Indo-Pacific partner countries, collectively known as the IP4: Australia, Japan, New Zealand, and South Korea. It may be tempting to see this as evidence that NATO-IP4 relations are on the downturn, but a deeper analysis does not support such a conclusion. First, the main variable affecting the presence of the IP4 leaders was not the interest of NATO and IP4 countries in continued engagement, but the nature of the summits themselves. In addition, it is not clear that regular leader-level attendance at annual NATO summits is still a necessary driver of NATO-IP4 relations. The logic for continued cooperation between NATO and the IP4 is as strong as ever in the current geopolitical climate. [...]
